title: Multiplication Facts (1-10)
description: Master multiplication facts 1-10 for Class 3. Learn commutative property, missing factor problems, and times tables. Free online tests and IMO practice.

topics.title: Multiplication Fluency (1x1 to 10x10)
topics.concept:
Multiplication is repeated addition. Knowing your times tables up to 10x10 is essential for all higher maths.

Key facts to memorize:

  • Any number x 1 = itself (7x1=7)
  • Any number x 10 = add a 0 (6x10=60)
  • 9x rule: digits of product sum to 9 (9x3=27, 2+7=9)
  • 5x rule: ends in 0 or 5 (5x7=35)

examples.solution: 56. 7x8 is one of the trickier facts. Remember: 56 = 7x8 (5,6,7,8 — the digits go in order!).
54. Use the 9s trick: 9x6=54, and 5+4=9. Always works for 9 times table.

recap: Practice all facts from 1x1 to 10x10 daily.
9x trick: digits of product always sum to 9.

topics.title: Commutative Property of Multiplication
topics.concept:
The commutative property means: order does not matter in multiplication.

a x b = b x a

This is useful because you only need to learn half the times table — if you know 7x8=56, you also know 8x7=56.

examples.solution: 6 x 5 = 30. Commutative property: switching the order gives the same answer.

examples.problem: Write another fact related to 8 x 3 = 24.
examples.solution: 3 x 8 = 24. Flip the two numbers — the product stays the same.
Yes. Both equal 63. Commutative property always works for multiplication.

recap: a x b = b x a always. Order never changes the product.
Knowing 7x8=56 means you also know 8x7=56 for free.
This halves the number of multiplication facts you need to memorize.

topics.title: Missing Factor Problems
topics.concept:
When you know the product (answer) and one factor, you can find the missing factor using division or the times table.

Example: ___ x 6 = 24. Think: what times 6 equals 24? 4 x 6 = 24, so the answer is 4.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 150' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' style='max-width:100%;font-family:sans-serif'><rect width='480' height='150' fill='#fef3c7' rx='10'/><text stroke="none" x='240' y='22' text-anchor='middle' font-size='14' fill='#374151' font-weight='bold'>___ x 6 = 42</text><text stroke="none" x='240' y='50' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12' fill='#374151'>Think: 6 x what = 42?</text><text stroke="none" x='80' y='75' font-size='11' fill='#374151'>6x5=30</text><text stroke="none" x='80' y='93' font-size='11' fill='#374151'>6x6=36</text><text stroke="none" x='80' y='111' font-size='13' fill='#10b981' font-weight='bold'>6x7=42</text><text stroke="none" x='200' y='95' font-size='18' fill='#10b981' font-weight='bold'>So answer = 7!</text><rect x='155' y='60' width='160' height='45' fill='#bbf7d0' stroke='#10b981' stroke-width='2' rx='6'/><text stroke="none" x='235' y='78' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12' fill='#065f46'>42 / 6 = 7</text><text stroke="none" x='235' y='96' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12' fill='#065f46'>Divide product by known factor</text><text stroke="none" x='240' y='140' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12' fill='#374151'>Missing factor = Product / Known factor</text></svg>

examples.solution: Think: 7 x what = 35? Count by 7s: 7,14,21,28,35. Five 7s = 35. Answer: 5. Or: 35/7 = 5.
54 / 9 = 6. Or count by 9s until you reach 54: 9,18,27,36,45,54 — that is 6 steps. Answer: 6.

recap: Use your times table knowledge to find the missing number.
Always check: missing factor x known factor = product.

quiz.q: To find a missing factor, you ___ the product by the known factor.

questions.explanation: 5 x 7 = 35. Five times table always ends in 0 or 5.

questions.q: By the commutative property, if 9 x 4 = 36, then 4 x 9 = ?
questions.explanation: Commutative: a x b = b x a. So 4 x 9 = 9 x 4 = 36.

questions.q: 6 x 8 = ___ x 6. What goes in the blank?
questions.explanation: By commutative property: 6 x 8 = 8 x 6. So blank = 8.

questions.q: Which is larger: 8 x 9 or 7 x 10?
If 6 x a = 54, what is a x 3?
questions.explanation: 6 x a = 54 means a = 9. So a x 3 = 9 x 3 = 27.

questions.q: A rectangular array has 7 rows and 8 columns. How many dots total?
Which product is a perfect square: 3x12, 4x9, 5x8, 6x7?
questions.explanation: 3x12=36=6x6 and 4x9=36=6x6. Both equal 36, which is a perfect square.
